title: jolt-2001-world
label: The Don

won.source: The fed's own title history names Cataclysm; the site's news post of 30 December 2001 says the transcript of Cataclysm was uploaded that day (/promotions/jolt-2001/archive/jolt-2001-news-and-updates-2002-01.html). The 2005 site's list of Season One's pay-per-views dates Cataclysm 31 December.

how: Won the vacant belt at Cataclysm, per the fed's own title history; he is champion on the 20 January 2002 card, where he retains by disqualification.

lost.source: The second season put the belt up again at Unwanted on 28 May 2002; no earlier loss survives.

note: Brandon Blade beat him by disqualification on 20 January 2002 and by pinfall in a non-title match on 3 February; The Don kept the belt. The second season's belt is a new one. Sources disagree on who held the belt: Unwanted's own opening video of 28 May 2002 shows the past champions as Brandon Blade, erØn and then 'Kodiak Vic Creed looking across the ring at The Don, as the golden title is slung across his broad shoulder' (/promotions/jolt-2001/archive/jolt-2001-unwanted-2002-05-28.html). The 2005 site's Tuesday Intense of 15 March 2005 replays the Cataclysm match as a 'jOlt Vintage Classics' segment that ends 'Winner, and new jOlt World Heavyweight Champion: Kodiak Vic Creed, winning with 10 points' (/promotions/jolt-2001/archive/jolt-2001-tuesday-intense-2005-03-15.html), and its Mardi Gras write-up of 23 January 2005 says of the belt's two versions 'We then used, for Kodiak Vic Creed and The Don’s reigns, the re-make' (/promotions/jolt-2001/archive/jolt-2001-mardi-gras-2005-01-23.html). The fed's own title history names no Kodiak Vic Creed reign. Each account is recorded; none is preferred.

title: jolt-2001-ambassador
label: Kenjiro Ito

won.source: The site's own WrestleSault I review, posted 1 March 2005 (/promotions/jolt-2001/archive/jolt-2001-column-6-2005-03-01.html): 'Ito's Ice Age gets the pin @ 7:08'. The Mardi Gras card and the review date WrestleSault 27 February 2005; the site's pay-per-view page says 'Sunday, February 28th'.

how: Beat Chris Mezz with Ito's Ice Age at WrestleSault I in Montreal, the match the pay-per-view page gave the Triple Crown semi-finals' runners-up; Jeff Garvin had beaten him in their semi-final earlier that night.

lost.source: No loss survives in the pages held. PTCpedia's Ito article (a secondary source, /promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-kenjiro-ito.html) says he lost it to Ken Kaze in a hardcore match at the Mayfall pay-per-view; fWo's own text of 4 July 2005 bills him the former Jolt Ambassador Champion.

note: Defences in the pages held: a no contest with Carson Nash in the main event of the 15 March 2005 Tuesday Night Intense, and a win over Amy 'Aimz' Campbell on PRIME Wrestling's ReVolution 58 of 16 March, reported on the site on 19 March. ACW's own write-up of Courage 75 has him keep it against Alias.

title: jolt-2001-triple-crown
label: Brandon Youngblood

won.source: The site's own WrestleSault I review, posted 1 March 2005 (/promotions/jolt-2001/archive/jolt-2001-column-6-2005-03-01.html): 'YOUNGBLOOD WITH A SPINEBUSTER FOR THE WIN @ 54:37', after which he 'recieves all three Jolt Triple Crown belts'.

how: Won the tournament final over Jeff Garvin at WrestleSault I in Montreal with a spinebuster after 54:37, the first Triple Crown Champion.

lost.source: On the 15 March 2005 Tuesday Night Intense the CEO's no-contact clause made any attack on Garvin a forfeit; Youngblood threw the belt down and attacked Garvin to save Melissa Garvin, and the page ends on the open question 'Did Brandon Youngblood willingly forfeit his Triple Crown Championship?'
